tools.name: get_estate_overview
tools.description: Every tower with its bundle, lifecycle state, open work, items awaiting approval, SLA attainment against target and glidepath against contract. Start here when a question is about the service as a whole or you do not yet know which tower it concerns.

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: What happened since the user's last session and what is waiting on them: items closed and closed unaided, hours displaced, incidents avoided, proposals raised, and the ranked asks (approvals, verifications, decisions, obligations, proposals), marked as the user's or another owner's.

tools.name: get_work_queue
tools.description: Open work items (incidents, requests, problems, changes, findings) with priority, state, SLA consumed and breach probability, most at risk first. Optionally narrowed to a tower, a priority or a state.

tools.name: get_work_item
tools.description: One work item by id or reference: its service, demand class, affected components, SLA clock, autonomy decision and timeline.

id.description: Work item id (wo_…) or its reference (INC…, RITM…)

tools.name: get_approvals
tools.description: Plans held at a human gate, ordered by SLA consumed: the action classes, blast radius, agent grades, the gate's approver role and timeout.

tools.name: get_sla
tools.description: Service levels and experience levels with month-to-date attainment against target, breaches, headroom and the credit bands at stake. Optionally for one tower.

tools.name: get_data_estate
tools.description: The data estate register: sources, feeds, pipelines, self-service workflows, datasets, semantic models, reports, operational applications and external recipients, with each item's own state against its contract, what reaches it from upstream, contract enforcement, classification, stewardship and lineage gaps. Breaches carry every consumer they make wrong (reports, applications, and external parties with the categories of personal data they receive) and the recovery path.

tools.name: get_data_item
tools.description: One data item by id or name: contract and its checks, freshness, runs, classification, steward, holds, lineage upstream and everything it feeds. External recipients carry the receiving party, the categories they receive and how often.

id.description: Data item id (e.g. ds_engagement_gold) or its name

tools.name: get_data_reliability
tools.description: Reliability of the data services over the last 30 days. services: each declared data service's tier, availability against its target, unplanned, planned and degraded minutes, error budget, any outage open now and the items upstream with no telemetry. tonight: each scheduled run's projected landing against its window from its duration trend, its margin, whether it is lengthening and how many days until it misses, whether an open failure blocks it, and capacity pressure on its platform. failures: every failed run, the error, how it was recovered (platform retry, agent, person, code change, or still open), by whom, minutes to restart and to landing, and whether it landed within its window. A run recovered within its window counts as on time.

service.description: A data service id (e.g. dsv_utilisation) or name, to read one service and its outages

tools.name: get_privacy_requests
tools.description: Access, erasure and retrieval requests against the statutory clock, with search gaps, process breaches, holds and retention. Give an id for one request's store-by-store search and actions, and the external recipients sent the person's records, with whether each has been told of an erasure.

tools.name: get_acceleration
tools.description: How the platform shortens each stage of the engagement — transition, run, improve, assure, renew or exit. Returns the engagements loaded and what has been ingested for each, the reusable service packs behind their service lines, the stages with how many accelerators are live, partial or not built in each, and every accelerator: what the platform does instead of the manual work, which agents do it, whose time it gives back (the client's people, the service, or both), how long that work takes without the platform and whose estimate that is, what the platform shows today, and whether that figure is measured here, projected, declared or not measured. Give a stage to read one. Figures are read for the engagement whose estate is ingested. A client role is shown only its own engagement's stages; the supplier's own bid stage is visible to supplier roles.

tools.name: get_commitments
tools.description: What the engagement has committed to and what the platform reads against each promise today. Per commitment: the promise, the stage it belongs to, the target and its date, where the engagement started from and whether that baseline was read from the client's own ticket history or declared by someone, the figure measured today with what it was read from, whether it is met, on track, behind, missed or not measurable, how far it is from the target, and what happens if it is missed. Also the extract the baselines came from — volumes, the scope rule, the themes of demand, every phrasing seen ten times or more, and what that extract will not support, so a promise the records cannot measure is refused rather than scored. Give an engagement id to read another client's commitments; an engagement with nothing ingested returns its promises and no figures.

tools.name: get_recommendations
tools.description: What the service proposed without being asked, read across both registers — agents' unprompted proposals about the estate and the innovation register — against the improvement dimensions the client's contract names. Per dimension: how many recommendations in the cadence window, how many in total, how long since the last one, the value realised, and whether it has gone silent. Per recommendation: what it is, who raised it and whether they were asked, when, what it projected and what it actually returned, and whether it is open, accepted, delivered, realised, declined or expired without anyone deciding. Also the two figures that cut both ways: dimensions nothing has been raised on, which is the supplier's to answer for, and recommendations that expired undecided, which is the client's. An engagement whose contract files no dimensions is not scored for cadence.

tools.name: get_procedures
tools.description: The maintenance procedures and runbooks the contract requires, and whether each is current. Returns the client's own procedure areas as its contract names them — and whether anyone has adopted that list against a clause yet, because coverage is not scored against a list nobody filed. Per area: whether a current procedure exists, and which. Per procedure: its version and state, the role answerable for it, who wrote it, when it was last reviewed and when the next review is due, whether it is overdue, the agents that execute it, the action classes it authorises, the verification pack that proves a run worked, where it is written down, and how many times the platform actually executed it in the window. Also the gaps (areas with nothing current), the drafts, the overdue ones, the dormant ones (current, authorised to act, and never executed — dead or being bypassed), the areas the contract names that the platform offers nothing for, and the standard areas the contract does not name.

area.description: Area id or name, to read one

tools.name: set_procedure_areas
tools.description: Adopt the client's procedure areas into the register, against the clause they come from. Give nothing but the engagement to adopt the list its contract already files, in the client's own words and order; give areas to state a different list. Sealed to the evidence chain with the adopter's name, because this sets what coverage is measured against. Refused without a clause reference, and refused where it would drop an area that current procedures are attached to — coverage must not improve by deleting the inconvenient row. The diff is shown before it is written.

engagement.description: Engagement id. Defaults to the engagement in view.

reference.description: The clause or attachment the list comes from. Defaults to the one the contract files.

areas.description: The client's areas, in its own words. Omit to adopt the list the contract files.

name.description: The client's own words for the area

maps_to.description: Standard area id the platform offers for it, e.g. sa_triage. Omit where nothing fits.

tools.name: review_procedure
tools.description: Record a review of one procedure: what changed or that nothing did, and the version it now stands at. Resets its review clock and seals the review to the evidence chain. Refused for a procedure that does not exist, and refused without stating what changed — a review that records nothing is not a review.
tools.describe: Record a review of {procedure} at version {version}: {changed}.

procedure.description: Procedure id or name, e.g. pr_handoff

version.description: The version it now stands at, e.g. 2.3

changed.description: What changed, or that nothing did

tools.name: get_successor_pack
tools.description: The pack a successor provider would start from, and whether it has ever been produced. Per part: what it is, what the successor can do with it on day one, the format, how many records it holds, whether it is the client's own knowledge coming home or the supplier's grant on exit, and the records it is built from. Also what the pack deliberately withholds and why, and every production of it with its manifest — part by part, the record count, the size and the digest sealed to the evidence chain. Use this when anyone asks what the client keeps if the supplier leaves, or how expensive leaving would be.

tools.name: produce_successor_pack
tools.description: Build the successor pack now: emits the content of every part, computes a digest over each and over the pack as a whole, and seals the manifest to the evidence chain. This is the difference between a pack that is counted and a pack that exists — a production can be run on any ordinary day, and the commitment that it is produced annually reads these records. The parts can then be downloaded from the pack page.
tools.describe: Produce the successor pack now and seal its manifest ({reason}).

reason.description: Why it is being produced: the annual proof, a benchmark review, or a real exit

tools.name: get_client_control
tools.description: What the client controls over the agent workforce. The rights the client holds — lowering what an agent may do, stopping one outright, withdrawing an action class across the workforce, and lifting any of those again — with the roles that hold each right, how much notice the supplier may require (none), who may lift it (the client, never the supplier) and what exercising it does not change. Then per agent: the ceiling the supplier granted, the ceiling the client has imposed, whether it is stopped, and what it may therefore actually do. Also the directives in force with who set each one and why, and when the right was last exercised.

tools.name: set_client_autonomy
tools.description: The client lowers what an agent may do, stops it outright, withdraws an action class across the workforce, or lifts a directive it set earlier. Takes effect immediately, with no notice to the supplier and no supplier approval in the path, and is sealed to the evidence chain. Held only by the client's own roles: a supplier role cannot call it, cannot exercise it on the client's behalf, and cannot lift what the client set. Service levels, charges and the glidepath commitment are unchanged by it — stopping an agent does not release the supplier from the work. Refused for a cap above what the supplier granted, which would be a grant rather than a restriction.
tools.describe: {kind} — {target} ({reason}). Takes effect immediately; service levels unchanged.

kind.description: Lower the ceiling, stop it outright, or lift a directive

scope.description: One agent, one action class across every agent, or every agent

target.description: Agent id or name, or an action class id such as AC-37. Omit for scope "all".

cap.description: The ceiling to impose, for kind "cap"

reason.description: Why, in the client's own words

tools.name: get_provenance
tools.description: Where the figures come from. Every dataset the platform reads with its origin — a file the client supplied, a record the platform itself wrote as it ran, a deterministic demonstration seed, or somebody's declaration — the source named precisely enough to be checked, when it was taken, the screens it feeds, what a reader must not use it for, and whether the capability behind it is live, partial or not built. Give a screen's path to read only what feeds that screen. Use this whenever anyone asks whether a figure is real, measured, this client's own, or demonstration data: answer from this register rather than from impression.

tools.name: record_commitment_remedy
tools.description: Record what has been decided about a commitment that is not being met: a recovery accepted with the date it lands, the contractual consequence applied, a re-baselining, or a waiver. Sealed to the evidence chain. Refused for a commitment that is met or on track, for a consequence the commitment does not carry, for a recovery dated in the past, and for a decision already recorded in the same terms. A commitment that is behind with nothing recorded counts as unanswered until one of these is.

detail.description: What was decided, in one clause

reference.description: Governance reference: minutes, change record or credit note

due.description: When an accepted recovery lands, as YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: get_agent_readiness
tools.description: What it takes to put an agent into service and whether each one is there yet. Per agent: the lifecycle stage it has reached (draft, evaluated, shadow, supervised, autonomous, or suspended), how many readiness checks pass, the next stage and exactly which checks stand in the way, the budget it has consumed, what it escalated to people over the last 30 days with the reason mix, the share of its runs that represents, how many are still waiting and the median pick-up time, and its set-up — identity and least-privilege scope, model, monthly budget, step limit per run, who it escalates to when context is missing, when the stop was last exercised, the change record its configuration was released under, and what it retrieves to know this client. Checks are grouped as build it, prove it, make it operational and watch it, and each names the record it was read from. Give an agent to read its full checklist; otherwise the fleet, with the checks failing across it and why agents escalate, each reason carrying what would fix it.

tools.name: get_exit_readiness
tools.description: Renew or exit: the months left on the term, the exit obligations with the clause behind each, its owner, whether it is ready and why, and what the platform itself holds of the client store by store — what each contains, where it is processed, how many records where they can be counted, whether it can be returned, whether it has been returned or destroyed, and what is retained with the reason and the date it falls away. Also the benchmark pack the ledger can evidence (quarters of contracted against actual reduction, baseline hours, service level attainment, banked hours) and the successor pack (verified assertions, demand classes, estate items, applications, runbook artefacts, evidence records).

tools.name: record_data_return
tools.description: Record that one of the platform's holdings has been returned to the client, with the reference of the handover. Sealed to the evidence chain. Refused for a holding that cannot be returned in a usable form.
tools.describe: Record that {holding_id} was returned to the client (reference {reference}).

holding_id.description: Holding id (e.g. hold_knowledge) or its name

tools.name: certify_destruction
tools.description: Certify that one of the platform's holdings has been destroyed, with the method and reference, and seal the certificate to the evidence chain. Refused where the holding is retained under a stated reason, or where it is returnable and has not been returned yet.

holding_id.description: Holding id (e.g. hold_context) or its name

method.description: How it was destroyed, e.g. crypto-erase of the index and its keys

tools.name: get_privacy_obligations
tools.description: incidents: data incidents touching the client's data, each against the 24-hour notice the contract requires to the client (hours left, or when and by whom it was notified and whether late), the client's own 72-hour clock to its regulator for personal data breaches, people involved, categories, and the external parties the data had reached. records: the records of processing, each checked against lineage: recipients the record declares against those lineage says it reaches, undeclared recipients, transfers outside an adequate country without a mechanism, whether a DPIA is required for special-category data and done, and stores without retention; plus external recipients no record declares.

tools.name: record_recipient_notice
tools.description: Record that a person told an external recipient of an erasure request, with the reference of the message sent. The platform does not contact the recipient; it records the notice and seals it to the evidence chain.
tools.describe: Record that {recipient_id} was told of erasure {request_id} (reference {reference}).

recipient_id.description: External recipient id (e.g. rc_health) or party name

tools.name: record_incident_notice
tools.description: Record the notice given to the client of a data incident, with its reference. Stops the contractual notice clock and seals the notice to the evidence chain. The client's own notice to its regulator is theirs to give.
tools.describe: Record that the client was notified of {incident_id} (reference {reference}).

reference.description: Reference of the notice sent to the client

tools.name: get_releases
tools.description: Vendor and internal releases across applications and the data estate: window, state, regression gate, blocking and informing flags, and change freezes.

tools.name: get_tech_debt
tools.description: The technical debt register with interest measured from the demand ledger, estimates, payback, flags, and the quarterly remediation recommendation within declared capacity.

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Service functions of a contract bundle and the agents that own or only assist each, derived from agent charters.

bundle.description: Bundle id, e.g. B3 or B4

tools.name: get_objectives
tools.description: The client's stated objectives with each measure resolved to its current value, target and state (on track, at risk, not measured), whether a measure is a proxy, acceptance, and the gaps each objective declares.

tools.name: get_programmes
tools.description: Programme burn-down: scope remaining when only evidenced completion counts against remaining if declarations are taken at face value, items declared but not evidenced, overdue items and the projected end.

tools.name: get_client_effort
tools.description: What the client declares about its own staff effort released to strategic work, per function: released and gained FTE, the strength of each declaration, and which are stale or never re-attested. Declared, not measured.

tools.name: get_deflection
tools.description: Demand deflection against signed baselines: the attributed rate beside the total fall, unexplained volume, classes withheld for short windows and baseline basis.

tools.name: get_headroom
tools.description: Growth headroom: whether business growth has been absorbed or the test is untested, forward headroom against declared drivers, and what is actually rising by cause.

tools.name: get_glidepath
tools.description: Productivity glidepath delivered against contract, per tower, with banked and verifying hours and the transform credit position including freezes.

tools.name: get_demand
tools.description: Costed demand classes from the demand ledger with annual volume, effort, trend, cause and elimination state, largest first. Optionally for one tower.

tools.name: get_proposals
tools.description: Open proposals the workforce raised: the claim, the authoring agent, the decision requested and when it expires.

tools.name: get_vendors
tools.description: Suppliers with contract, support tier, contracted response, applications supplied, work held on them and renewal dates.

tools.name: get_work_orders
tools.description: Separately authorised development orders against applications and data items: state, authorisation, estimate, burn and flags such as unauthorised delivery or overrun.

tools.name: get_portfolio
tools.description: The application portfolio reconciled against the client's own record: count under support (a floor), agreement share, incidents in dispute, configuration drift and ungoverned embedded AI.

tools.name: get_agents
tools.description: The agent fleet, the platform's and the client's: state, autonomy ceiling, towers, live success, drift alarms, cost and incidents.

tools.name: get_autonomy
tools.description: Autonomy posture by tower and action class where the current level is below target, with the blocker. Optionally for one tower.

tools.name: get_ai_incidents
tools.description: AI incidents — fabrication, injection, oversight and cohort findings — with severity, state and the notification and root-cause clocks.

tools.name: get_missions
tools.description: Standing missions: goal, tower, workforce, state and budget used.

tools.name: search_evidence
tools.description: Search the sealed evidence chain by record id, work item, agent, action class, actor or words in the summary. Returns the latest matches.

tools.name: get_my_workplace
tools.description: For the service consumer: open issues affecting the systems they use, the self-service routes genuinely available for what they raise, and how the service is running for their cohort.

tools.name: get_verification_queue
tools.description: Knowledge assertions not yet human-verified: the claim, tower, tier, confidence and verification state.

tools.name: decide_proposal
tools.description: Accept or reject an open proposal the workforce raised, with a note. Recorded under the user's name.

tools.name: set_brake
tools.description: Apply or release the global autonomy brake. Applied, every agent drops to Advise platform-wide and work continues through humans.

tools.name: suspend_agent
tools.description: Suspend one agent, with the reason. A suspended agent takes no work until reinstated.

tools.name: reinstate_agent
tools.description: Reinstate a suspended agent.

tools.name: declare_major_incident
tools.description: Declare a major incident on a work item. Autonomy caps to Advise platform-wide while it is open, and an incident conversation opens.

tools.name: run_conformance
tools.description: Run the contract-conformance set against the deployed policy engine and record the result: each commitment, expected and observed decision, and whether it holds.
tools.describe: Run the conformance set and record the result under your name.

tools.name: accept_objective
tools.description: Accept an objective with its measures and declared gaps, sealing it under the user's name. Only a client-side role should accept.
tools.describe: Accept objective {id} with its measures and gaps.

tools.name: verify_assertion
tools.description: Verify, correct or reject a knowledge assertion. A correction states the right claim.

tools.name: run_agent
tools.description: Hand an operational intent to the agent runtime: an agent is routed, retrieves context, reasons, and if the estate must change proposes a plan that the Autonomy Policy Engine decides — advise, a human gate, supervised or autonomous. Use for diagnosing a live problem in depth or remediating one. The run narrates itself and returns its finding, mode and outcome.
tools.describe: Hand “{intent}” to the agent runtime. If it proposes a change, the policy engine decides whether it runs.

intent.description: The intent in the operator's words

tools.name: approve_gate
tools.description: Approve a plan held at a human gate. The approval is sealed to the evidence chain under the user's name.

tools.name: reject_gate
tools.description: Reject a plan held at a human gate, with the reason. The work returns to the human queue and the disagreement is scored against the agent.
